unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: Which component in the Von Neumann architecture coordinates and sequences operations across all components?
explanation: The Control Unit (CU) decodes program instructions and generates control timing signals that synchronize CPU and system operations.
topic_title: Von Neumann Architecture & Stored Program Concept

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: Which computer generation introduced Integrated Circuits (ICs) replacing discrete transistors?
explanation: Third generation computers (1964-1971) incorporated ICs developed by Jack Kilby and Robert Noyce, drastically improving speed and shrinking machine size.
topic_title: Computer Generations (1st to 5th Generation) & Evolution

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: The key electronic component of First Generation computers was:
explanation: First-generation computers (1940-1956) like ENIAC and UNIVAC utilized vacuum tubes (thermionic valves) as primary switching and memory elements.
topic_title: Computer Generations (1st to 5th Generation) & Evolution

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: VLSI (Very Large Scale Integration) and ULSI technologies were primarily introduced in which generation?
explanation: Fourth generation computers utilized VLSI (thousands of transistors on a chip) and later ULSI, leading to modern single-chip microprocessors.
topic_title: Computer Generations (1st to 5th Generation) & Evolution

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: Which register holds the memory address of the next instruction to be fetched and executed?
explanation: The Program Counter (PC) automatically holds and increments the memory address of the next sequential machine instruction to execute.
topic_title: Memory Hierarchy: Registers, Cache, RAM (SRAM/DRAM), ROM (PROM/EPROM/EEPROM)

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: In the instruction execution cycle, the correct sequential order of phases is:
explanation: The instruction machine cycle strictly follows: Fetch from memory -> Decode opcode -> Execute ALU/Control operation -> Store result back to register/memory.
topic_title: Instruction Execution Cycle (Fetch, Decode, Execute, Store)

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: What architecture features physically separate memory and buses for program instructions and data storage?
explanation: Harvard architecture provides dedicated, separate address and data paths for instructions and data, allowing simultaneous memory access.
topic_title: Secondary Storage: Magnetic Disks, Optical Disks, Flash Storage & SSDs

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: The 'Von Neumann Bottleneck' refers to throughput limitations caused by:

options.text: Slow clock speeds in the ALU
Sharing a single bus between CPU and memory for both data and code
Lack of registers in the Control Unit

explanation: The Von Neumann bottleneck occurs because program memory and data memory share the same physical bus, constraining CPU execution to bus transfer rates.
topic_title: Von Neumann Architecture & Stored Program Concept

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: Which classification of computers is designed specifically to process intensive mathematical calculations like weather modeling and nuclear simulations?
explanation: Supercomputers (e.g., PARAM Siddhi, Fugaku) are engineered with thousands of parallel processing units specifically for ultra-high compute workloads.
topic_title: Classification of Computers (Micro, Mini, Mainframe, Supercomputer, Distributed & Parallel)

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: Computers that handle large-scale enterprise transaction processing and serve thousands of simultaneous online users are known as:
explanation: Mainframe computers (e.g., IBM zSeries) excel in massive I/O throughput, continuous uptime, and enterprise batch and transaction processing.
topic_title: Classification of Computers (Micro, Mini, Mainframe, Supercomputer, Distributed & Parallel)

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: Which type of computer memory is fastest and placed closest to the CPU execution core?
explanation: Internal CPU registers operate directly at the processor's core clock speed (picoseconds access time), making them the fastest storage element in the hierarchy.
topic_title: Memory Hierarchy: Registers, Cache, RAM (SRAM/DRAM), ROM (PROM/EPROM/EEPROM)

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: SRAM (Static RAM) differs fundamentally from DRAM (Dynamic RAM) because SRAM:

options.text: Is made of flip-flops and does not require periodic capacitor refreshing
Is cheaper per megabyte than DRAM

explanation: SRAM uses 4 to 6 transistors configured as a bistable latch (flip-flop) to store bits without capacitor refresh cycles, making it significantly faster and ideal for CPU caches.
topic_title: Memory Hierarchy: Registers, Cache, RAM (SRAM/DRAM), ROM (PROM/EPROM/EEPROM)

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: Why does DRAM require continuous memory refresh cycles?

options.text: Because its memory cells store charge on microscopic capacitors that leak voltage over time
To clean up invalid memory addresses
To synchronize with hard disk spin rates

explanation: Each DRAM memory cell consists of a single transistor and capacitor; the capacitor leaks electrical charge and must be rewritten thousands of times per second.
topic_title: Memory Hierarchy: Registers, Cache, RAM (SRAM/DRAM), ROM (PROM/EPROM/EEPROM)

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: Which type of Read-Only Memory can be erased electrically in-circuit without removing the chip or using ultraviolet light?
explanation: EEPROM (Electrically Erasable Programmable ROM) and Flash memory can be wiped and reprogrammed byte-by-byte using electrical voltage signals directly in circuit.
topic_title: Memory Hierarchy: Registers, Cache, RAM (SRAM/DRAM), ROM (PROM/EPROM/EEPROM)

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: What type of ROM requires exposure to intense Ultraviolet (UV) light through a quartz window for erasure?
explanation: EPROM (Erasable PROM) chips feature a distinctive transparent quartz window on top through which UV light is beamed for 15-20 minutes to erase bit patterns.
topic_title: Memory Hierarchy: Registers, Cache, RAM (SRAM/DRAM), ROM (PROM/EPROM/EEPROM)

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: Cache memory is introduced in computer systems primarily to:

options.text: Expand the physical storage capacity of secondary hard drives
Bridge the significant operating speed disparity between the fast CPU and slower DRAM main memory
Protect the operating system from virus infection

explanation: Cache memory stores recently and frequently accessed instructions and data to minimize CPU wait states caused by the relatively slow access times of DRAM.
topic_title: Memory Hierarchy: Registers, Cache, RAM (SRAM/DRAM), ROM (PROM/EPROM/EEPROM)

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: The principle underlying effective cache memory operation, where recently accessed data items are likely to be accessed again soon, is known as:
explanation: Temporal locality states that an instruction or memory location referenced at time t will very likely be re-referenced in the near future (e.g. inside loop bodies).
topic_title: Memory Hierarchy: Registers, Cache, RAM (SRAM/DRAM), ROM (PROM/EPROM/EEPROM)

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: Spatial locality of reference describes the phenomenon where:

options.text: Data stored at distant server nodes is accessed fastest
Accessing a memory address increases the probability that adjacent memory addresses will be accessed soon
Only read operations are performed in memory
Code is kept in optical media for longevity

explanation: Spatial locality exploits the contiguous storage of program code and array elements: loading an entire cache line brings neighboring bytes that the CPU will execute next.
topic_title: Memory Hierarchy: Registers, Cache, RAM (SRAM/DRAM), ROM (PROM/EPROM/EEPROM)

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: Non-volatile storage media refers to storage that:

options.text: Loses its data immediately when electrical power is switched off
Retains its stored information even when the computer system is completely powered down
Cannot be written to more than once
Operates exclusively in magnetic tape formats

explanation: Non-volatile memory (such as ROM, HDD, SSD, USB flash drives) retains stored binary data indefinitely without requiring continuous power supply.
topic_title: Secondary Storage: Magnetic Disks, Optical Disks, Flash Storage & SSDs

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: Solid State Drives (SSDs) outperform traditional Hard Disk Drives (HDDs) because SSDs:

options.text: Use spinning magnetic platters with faster read/write heads
Have no moving mechanical parts and utilize high-speed NAND flash memory
Store data in analog signals rather than digital bits
Rely entirely on static RAM chips with battery backup

explanation: SSDs contain zero spinning disks or mechanical actuator arms, eliminating seek latency and rotational delay through parallel non-volatile NAND flash channels.
topic_title: Secondary Storage: Magnetic Disks, Optical Disks, Flash Storage & SSDs

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: Software etched permanently into hardware ROM/flash chips during manufacture to control low-level device initialization is:
explanation: Firmware (such as the motherboard UEFI/BIOS) provides essential machine-level control programs burned into non-volatile memory.
topic_title: Computer Languages: Machine Language, Assembly Language, High-Level Languages

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: Software distributed freely on a trial basis for evaluation, requiring payment or license purchase after a grace period, is called:
explanation: Shareware is commercial software distributed at no cost for a trial period (e.g., 30 days) to allow evaluation before purchasing a full license.
topic_title: Software Licensing Models: Demoware, Shareware, Freeware, Firmware, Free & Open Source

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: Demoware is best described as:

options.text: Software that works only when connected to a demonstration server
Commercial software distributed with disabled key features (e.g., cannot save or export) to showcase capabilities
Software made specifically for classroom teaching
Free software with unlimited commercial distribution rights

explanation: Demoware is a restricted software build where vital features (like file saving, export, or advanced filters) are locked until the full commercial product is bought.
topic_title: Software Licensing Models: Demoware, Shareware, Freeware, Firmware, Free & Open Source

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: Which category of software is responsible for controlling computer hardware resources and providing a platform for application software to run?
explanation: System software comprises the Operating System, device drivers, and core utilities that manage CPU scheduling, memory, file systems, and hardware peripherals.
topic_title: Types of Software: System Software, Application Software & Utility Software

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: Disk Cleanup, Disk Defragmenter, and Antivirus scanners are classified as:
explanation: Utility software consists of system maintenance and optimization programs that analyze, configure, optimize, or protect computer hardware and files.
topic_title: Definition & Characteristics of Computers

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: Free Software, as championed by Richard Stallman and the Free Software Foundation (FSF), emphasizes:

options.text: Zero cost of purchase above all else
The user's liberty to run, study, modify, and redistribute the program source code

explanation: Free software ('free as in speech, not free beer') guarantees the four essential freedoms: to run, study source code, redistribute copies, and distribute modified versions.
topic_title: Software Licensing Models: Demoware, Shareware, Freeware, Firmware, Free & Open Source

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: Open-source software licenses typically mandate that:

options.text: The source code must be made accessible to users alongside the binary executable
Users cannot modify the program under any circumstance
The software can never be run on commercial operating systems
Only university researchers are allowed to download the program

explanation: Open-source software (OSS) licenses ensure that human-readable source code is distributed openly, permitting collective inspection, peer review, and community enhancement.
topic_title: Software Licensing Models: Demoware, Shareware, Freeware, Firmware, Free & Open Source

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: Which of the following is considered System Software?
explanation: Microsoft Windows 11 is an Operating System, which is the foundational system software managing all computing hardware and user applications.
topic_title: Types of Software: System Software, Application Software & Utility Software

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: Proprietary software is software that:

options.text: Is placed into the public domain with no copyright restrictions
Has its source code kept secret and legally protected by copyright and end-user license agreements (EULA)
Can be freely decompiled and resold by any purchaser
Is funded exclusively by educational grants

explanation: Proprietary (closed-source) software remains the intellectual property of its creator; users obtain only an executable license without source code access.
topic_title: Software Licensing Models: Demoware, Shareware, Freeware, Firmware, Free & Open Source

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: Software distributed at zero financial cost but where the author retains all copyright and does NOT provide access to source code is:
explanation: Freeware is available free of charge for use, but its proprietary source code is closed and users may not alter, decompile, or sell it.
topic_title: Software Licensing Models: Demoware, Shareware, Freeware, Firmware, Free & Open Source

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: Machine language is composed exclusively of:

options.text: Mnemonic operation codes like ADD and MOV
Binary patterns of 0s and 1s understood directly by the CPU

explanation: Machine code is the native first-generation programming language comprised directly of binary bits that electronic CPU logic gates decode and execute.
topic_title: Computer Languages: Machine Language, Assembly Language, High-Level Languages

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: Assembly language introduced human-readable abbreviations for machine instructions known as:
explanation: Assembly language replaces cryptic binary opcodes with symbolic mnemonics (such as MOV, ADD, SUB, JMP) to make low-level programming manageable.
topic_title: Computer Languages: Machine Language, Assembly Language, High-Level Languages

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: A language translator that converts entire high-level language source code into machine/object code in a single comprehensive pass is a(n):
explanation: A compiler analyzes and translates the entire source code file as a whole into an executable object module, producing error lists for the complete file.
topic_title: Translators: Assemblers, Compilers, Interpreters, Linkers & Loaders

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: An interpreter differs from a compiler because an interpreter:

options.text: Produces an independent .exe file that runs without the translator
Translates and executes source code line-by-line, halting immediately when an error is encountered
Only works with assembly language programs
Translates machine code back into high-level source code

explanation: An interpreter executes high-level statements sequentially in real time without creating an intermediate standalone binary file.
topic_title: Translators: Assemblers, Compilers, Interpreters, Linkers & Loaders

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: The translator tool specifically designed to convert Assembly Language programs into machine language is called a(n):
explanation: An assembler translates assembly language symbolic mnemonics and memory labels into equivalent binary machine opcodes and addresses.
topic_title: Translators: Assemblers, Compilers, Interpreters, Linkers & Loaders

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: What system utility takes one or more compiled object modules and resolves external library references into a single executable file?
explanation: The Linker connects compiled object files with required standard library routines (e.g. C standard library) and resolves cross-module memory references.
topic_title: Translators: Assemblers, Compilers, Interpreters, Linkers & Loaders

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: The software component that places an executable program from secondary storage into main memory (RAM) ready for CPU execution is the:
explanation: The Loader allocates memory space, reads executable machine code from disk into RAM, adjusts base addresses if necessary, and branches CPU control to main().
topic_title: Translators: Assemblers, Compilers, Interpreters, Linkers & Loaders

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: Which of the following is considered a Low-Level Language?
explanation: Assembly Language is a low-level language because it possesses a 1-to-1 correspondence with CPU hardware architecture and memory addressing.
topic_title: Computer Languages: Machine Language, Assembly Language, High-Level Languages

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: High-level programming languages (like C, Java, Python) are advantageous primarily because they:

options.text: Execute faster than raw machine code without translation
Are machine-independent, portable across different hardware platforms, and human-readable
Directly manipulate microprocessor registers without abstraction

explanation: High-level languages provide abstraction over CPU instruction sets, enabling software developers to write readable, portable code across varied CPU types.
topic_title: Computer Languages: Machine Language, Assembly Language, High-Level Languages

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: Characteristics of a good programming language include all of the following EXCEPT:

options.text: High portability and robust error-handling mechanisms
Complete hardware-dependence requiring total rewrite for each new computer model
Rich library support and expressive data structures

explanation: A good language prioritizes machine independence and portability so that algorithms run across diverse hardware without complete codebase rewrites.
topic_title: Definition & Characteristics of Computers

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: An algorithm is formally defined as:

options.text: A syntax error in computer code
A finite, unambiguous, step-by-step sequence of instructions designed to solve a specific computational problem
A hardware circuit for performing floating-point division
A graphical diagram representing data cables

explanation: An algorithm is an unambiguous, finite procedure that takes inputs, processes them through well-defined steps, and terminates with correct outputs.
topic_title: Problem-Solving Tools: Algorithms, Flowcharts, Pseudo-code & Characteristics of Good Languages

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: Which algorithmic property mandates that an algorithm must always terminate after a countable, finite number of operational steps?
explanation: Finiteness requires that for all valid input cases, the algorithm's execution terminates and does not run into an infinite loop.
topic_title: Problem-Solving Tools: Algorithms, Flowcharts, Pseudo-code & Characteristics of Good Languages

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: The algorithmic property 'Definiteness' means that:

options.text: Every operation must be clear, precise, and completely unambiguous with exactly one interpretation
The algorithm must use floating-point numbers
The code must run in under one second
The algorithm must produce multiple diverse answers

explanation: Definiteness requires that every instruction must be stated so clearly that human or machine can carry it out without ambiguity.
topic_title: Problem-Solving Tools: Algorithms, Flowcharts, Pseudo-code & Characteristics of Good Languages

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: In standard flowchart design, an Oval / Rounded Rectangle symbol represents:
explanation: The oval/pill symbol is the terminal symbol marking the starting entry point and termination end points of a flowchart.
topic_title: Problem-Solving Tools: Algorithms, Flowcharts, Pseudo-code & Characteristics of Good Languages

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: Which geometric shape is utilized in flowcharts to denote an Input or Output operation (e.g. Read X, Print Sum)?
explanation: A parallelogram represents input and output operations, such as receiving user data from keyboard or displaying results on a monitor.
topic_title: Problem-Solving Tools: Algorithms, Flowcharts, Pseudo-code & Characteristics of Good Languages

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: In a flowchart, a Diamond (Rhombus) symbol denotes a:

options.text: Decision / Conditional Branching point with two or more outgoing paths

explanation: A diamond shape evaluates a logical or relational condition (e.g., Is X > Y?) with exiting True/False or Yes/No branching paths.
topic_title: Problem-Solving Tools: Algorithms, Flowcharts, Pseudo-code & Characteristics of Good Languages

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: A small Circle symbol in a flowchart is used as a:

options.text: On-page connector linking interrupted flow lines

explanation: A small circle connector merges flow lines or continues a complex diagram to another section of the same page without crisscrossing lines.
topic_title: Problem-Solving Tools: Algorithms, Flowcharts, Pseudo-code & Characteristics of Good Languages

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: Pseudocode is best defined as:

options.text: Compiled binary code ready for CPU execution
An informal, human-readable high-level description of an algorithm that blends English with structured programming syntax
A computer virus disguised as a valid program

explanation: Pseudocode outlines algorithmic logic using human language and programming keywords (IF, WHILE, REPEAT) without strict syntax constraints.
topic_title: Problem-Solving Tools: Algorithms, Flowcharts, Pseudo-code & Characteristics of Good Languages

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: Which flowchart symbol represents processing or data calculation (such as Sum = A + B)?
explanation: A standard rectangle represents internal computational processing, variable manipulation, or assignment operations.
topic_title: Problem-Solving Tools: Algorithms, Flowcharts, Pseudo-code & Characteristics of Good Languages

unit_title: Computers Evolution, Architecture, Memory & Software Types
prompt: Top-down structured programming strategy involves:

options.text: Writing machine code first and high-level code later
Decomposing a complex system into progressively smaller, self-contained modular sub-problems and functions
Running software without testing individual modules
Storing all program variables in a single global file

explanation: Top-down design starts with the high-level objective and hierarchically breaks it down into manageable functional subroutines and modules.
topic_title: Problem-Solving Tools: Algorithms, Flowcharts, Pseudo-code & Characteristics of Good Languages

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: What is the primary objective of an Operating System?

options.text: To compile high-level source code into assembly
To manage computer hardware and provide a convenient platform for user programs

explanation: An Operating System acts as an intermediary between the computer user and computer hardware, managing hardware resources efficiently and comfortably.

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: The core program of an Operating System that remains continuously resident in main memory is known as the:
explanation: The Kernel is the central, foundational module of an OS that manages system resources (CPU scheduling, memory management, I/O) directly at the hardware layer.

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: Which software component interprets user commands entered via keyboard and conveys them to the OS kernel?
explanation: The Shell is the user interface program (CLI or GUI) that reads user commands, interprets them, and calls underlying kernel system routines.

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: An operating system architecture that allows two or more user processes to reside simultaneously in memory and share the CPU is called:
explanation: Multiprogramming keeps multiple jobs resident in memory simultaneously; when one job waits for I/O, the CPU executes another job, maximizing CPU utilization.

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: Time-sharing operating systems are fundamentally based on which scheduling concept?

options.text: First Come First Served without preemption
Multitasking with small CPU time slices (quanta) allocated cyclically to each active process
Executing only one job until completion

explanation: Time-sharing allocates a small slice of CPU execution time (quantum) to each active user/task rapidly, creating the illusion of simultaneous interactive execution.

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: In a Real-Time Operating System (RTOS), the defining performance parameter is:

options.text: Strict predictability and meeting hard deterministic execution deadlines

explanation: An RTOS guarantees completion of critical computational tasks within predetermined, rigid time constraints (deadlines).

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: Which type of real-time system considers a deadline miss as a catastrophic total system failure?
explanation: In Hard Real-Time systems (e.g., flight control, pacemaker implants, missile guidance), missing a deadline results in complete operational catastrophe.

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: Multithreading within an operating system allows:

options.text: Multiple CPUs to share a single keyboard
A single process to divide execution into multiple concurrent lightweight threads of control sharing memory
Connecting multiple printers to one computer
Simultaneous installation of two operating systems

explanation: A thread is a lightweight unit of CPU utilization; multithreading enables concurrent paths of execution within the same process address space.

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: What differentiates Multiprocessing from Multiprogramming?

options.text: Multiprocessing uses two or more physical CPUs or execution cores executing instructions simultaneously

explanation: Multiprocessing involves true parallel execution across multiple physical microprocessors/cores, whereas multiprogramming interweaves jobs on a single CPU.

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: In a modern OS, Spooling (Simultaneous Peripheral Operations On-Line) is most frequently used for:

options.text: Buffering print jobs on disk so the CPU can resume other tasks while the slow printer outputs data

explanation: SPOOLing intercepts print jobs sent by high-speed CPUs and stages them in temporary disk queues, freeing applications immediately.

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: A computer virus is formally classified as:

options.text: A hardware glitch caused by power surges
A malicious program designed to copy itself, attach to other programs, and alter or damage system operation without consent

explanation: A computer virus is human-written malicious code that infects host files, propagates self-replicating copies, and executes unauthorized destructive payloads.

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: Which type of computer virus infects the Master Boot Record (MBR) or partition table of storage disks?
explanation: Boot Sector viruses (e.g. Brain, Michelangelo) overwrite the MBR or partition boot record, executing malicious code every time the computer boots before the OS loads.

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: Viruses embedded within automated document scripts in applications like Microsoft Word or Excel are called:
explanation: Macro viruses are written in application macro languages (like VBA) and infect templates and spreadsheets, executing automatically when documents open.

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: A virus that changes its internal binary signature and decryption algorithm each time it replicates to evade detection is a:
explanation: Polymorphic viruses use a variable mutation engine and randomized encryption keys so that traditional signature-based antivirus scanners fail to recognize them.

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: What key characteristic distinguishes a Computer Worm from a Computer Virus?

options.text: A worm requires a human host file to attach to, whereas a virus spreads alone
A worm is completely self-contained and replicates autonomously across networks without needing a host program file
A worm only attacks Linux systems

explanation: Unlike a virus which requires a carrier host file (like an .exe), a worm operates independently, actively scanning network ports to propagate autonomously.

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: A malicious program disguised as legitimate, harmless software (such as a free game or utility) to trick users into installing it is a:
explanation: A Trojan Horse conceals a covert malicious payload inside an apparently useful application; it does not replicate like a virus, but grants backdoor access.

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: Malware that encrypts user data files and demands financial payment for the decryption key is termed:
explanation: Ransomware (e.g. WannaCry) maliciously encrypts user files using strong cryptography and demands ransom payment (typically in cryptocurrency).

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: Antivirus heuristic analysis refers to:

options.text: Comparing file hashes against a fixed database of known virus strings
Analyzing code structure and suspicious runtime behavioral patterns to detect novel, previously unknown malware
Cleaning physical dust from motherboard fans
Scanning optical DVDs with laser light

explanation: Heuristic analysis detects zero-day threats by identifying suspicious behavior (like modifying boot records or injecting code) rather than waiting for exact signature matches.

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: The process of isolating an infected or suspicious file into a secure directory where it cannot execute or spread is called:
explanation: Antivirus quarantine isolates suspicious binaries in an encrypted, permission-restricted directory preventing execution while preserving files for analysis.

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: Which historic program is widely recognized as the first PC computer virus (created in 1986)?
explanation: The 'Brain' virus, created in 1986 by Basit and Amjad Farooq Alvi in Pakistan, was the first boot sector virus for IBM PC-compatible DOS systems.

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: MS-DOS is functionally characterized as a:
explanation: MS-DOS is a 16-bit, single-user, single-tasking OS with a text-based Command Line Interface (CLI) that executes one foreground task at a time.

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: Which MS-DOS system file contains hardware-dependent device drivers and BIOS interface routines?
explanation: IO.SYS contains low-level hardware interface routines and device drivers that communicate directly with motherboard ROM-BIOS routines.

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: Which MS-DOS file serves as the core operating system kernel managing file access, memory allocation, and system services?
explanation: MSDOS.SYS is the DOS kernel, providing the DOS Application Programming Interface (API) via interrupt INT 21h for file manipulation and process execution.

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: COMMAND.COM in MS-DOS is responsible for:

options.text: Interpreting user commands, displaying the command prompt, and executing internal commands

explanation: COMMAND.COM is the default DOS command interpreter containing built-in internal routines (DIR, COPY, CLS) and launching external executables.

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: What is the traditional file naming convention enforced by MS-DOS (FAT16/FAT12)?

options.text: 8.3 rule (maximum 8-character filename followed by an optional 3-character extension)

explanation: MS-DOS strictly enforces the 8.3 filename structure: up to 8 alphanumeric characters, a period separator, and an optional 3-character extension (e.g. FILENAME.TXT).

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: In MS-DOS, the root directory of a drive is represented by which symbol?
explanation: The backslash character (\) designates the root directory of the active drive (e.g., C:\) in DOS and Windows paths.

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: The File Allocation Table (FAT) in DOS file systems functions as a:

options.text: Map of disk clusters recording which clusters hold parts of which files and identifying bad/free blocks

explanation: The FAT is a linked-allocation table mapping data clusters on disk, recording sequential cluster chains for files and tracking free or bad sectors.

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: Cold Booting a computer system refers to:

options.text: Restarting the computer using the Ctrl + Alt + Delete key combination
Starting the computer from a completely powered-off state by turning on the electrical power switch
Cooling the computer with ice packs
Running an antivirus in safe mode

explanation: A cold boot (hard boot) begins from zero electrical power, triggering full power supply stabilization, hardware reset lines, and comprehensive POST testing.

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: Warm Booting (Soft Boot) in MS-DOS is initiated by pressing:
explanation: Pressing Ctrl + Alt + Delete triggers a warm restart without cutting electrical power, bypassing prolonged hardware cold-start power cycles.

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: Which file is executed automatically by MS-DOS at the conclusion of the boot process to configure system startup settings and paths?
explanation: AUTOEXEC.BAT (Automatic Execute Batch file) runs automatically after COMMAND.COM loads, setting environment variables (PATH, PROMPT) and auto-starting utilities.

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: What distinguishes an Internal DOS command from an External DOS command?

options.text: Internal commands run on floppy disks; external run on hard disks
Internal commands are built directly into COMMAND.COM in memory; external commands exist as separate executable files (.COM, .EXE, .BAT) on disk
Internal commands are written in C; external are in Pascal
Internal commands cannot be run from prompt

explanation: Internal commands (like DIR, CLS, COPY) reside permanently in RAM within COMMAND.COM; external commands (like FORMAT.COM, CHKDSK.EXE) must be loaded from disk storage.

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: Which of the following is an INTERNAL DOS command?
explanation: DIR is an internal command built directly into COMMAND.COM and executes instantly without requiring secondary disk file lookup.

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: Which of the following is an EXTERNAL DOS command?
explanation: CHKDSK (Check Disk) is an external utility stored on disk as CHKDSK.EXE, used to inspect file system integrity and cluster allocation.

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: In MS-DOS, which command is used to remove an empty subdirectory?
explanation: The RD (Remove Directory) or RMDIR command deletes specified subdirectories, provided the directory is completely empty of files.

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: To view the text content of a file directly on screen in MS-DOS, the appropriate command is:
explanation: The TYPE command displays the unformatted text contents of a file on the standard console display (e.g. TYPE NOTES.TXT).

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: Which DOS command displays or modifies the read-only, archive, hidden, and system file attributes?
explanation: The external command ATTRIB sets (+R, +A, +S, +H) or clears (-R, -A, -S, -H) file flags for Read-only, Archive, System, and Hidden files.

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: To copy an entire directory tree including all nested subdirectories and files, the recommended DOS command is:
explanation: XCOPY (Extended Copy) can recursively traverse and copy directory hierarchies, subdirectories, and multiple files in a single invocation.

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: Which command in MS-DOS is used to clear the console monitor screen and return the prompt to the top-left corner?
explanation: CLS (Clear Screen) is an internal command that erases all console text lines and repositions the cursor at line 1, column 1.

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: In DOS command syntax, wildcards '*' and '?' represent:

options.text: '*' matches any sequence of characters; '?' matches exactly one single character
'*' matches one character; '?' matches any sequence
Both are used exclusively for mathematical calculations

explanation: In DOS file pattern matching, '?' matches any single character (e.g. T?ST.TXT matches TEST.TXT, TOST.TXT) while '*' matches any string of characters (e.g. *.DOC).

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: Which DOS command checks disk structure, repairs directory errors, and reports total and free disk memory?
explanation: CHKDSK examines the disk surface and FAT tables, displaying reports on total disk capacity, hidden files, allocation unit sizes, and remaining free bytes.

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: What is the primary role of the Windows Graphical User Interface (GUI)?

options.text: To force users to memorize terminal commands
To enable visual interaction using graphical icons, windows, menus, and a mouse pointer (WIMP interface)
To eliminate the need for computer RAM
To prevent connecting to the Internet

explanation: A GUI replaces cryptic typed commands with intuitive visual metaphors: Windows, Icons, Menus, and Pointer (WIMP).

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: In Windows, the horizontal bar typically positioned at the bottom of the screen displaying the Start button and active application tabs is the:
explanation: The Taskbar provides quick access to the Start menu, running application windows, pinned shortcuts, and the system notification area (system tray).

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: Which key combination in Windows allows users to instantly switch between active open application windows?
explanation: Pressing Alt + Tab displays the task-switching overlay, allowing rapid cyclical navigation among all open application windows.

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: What Windows utility is primarily designed for navigating, organizing, copying, and managing files and folders across drives?
explanation: Windows Explorer (File Explorer) is the core file manager providing hierarchical navigation of drives, folders, libraries, and files.

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: When a file is deleted in Windows using the Delete key, where is it temporarily stored for potential recovery?
explanation: The Recycle Bin acts as a safety holding area on disk, allowing deleted files to be restored to their original location before permanent purging.

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: To permanently delete a file in Windows without moving it to the Recycle Bin, which keyboard combination is used?
explanation: Shift + Delete completely bypasses the Recycle Bin, permanently deallocating the file clusters immediately.

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: Which Windows administrative tool allows users to configure hardware devices, adjust display settings, manage user accounts, and install network printers?
explanation: Control Panel (and Settings) centralizes configuration applets for hardware, network adapters, sound profiles, security, and peripheral drivers.

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: What utility in Windows displays active running processes, CPU utilization, memory allocation, and allows closing unresponsive frozen applications?
explanation: Task Manager (Ctrl + Shift + Esc) provides real-time telemetry on CPU, memory, disk, and network performance and allows terminating hanging processes.

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: A shortcut icon on the Windows desktop is characterized by:

options.text: A small curved arrow in the lower-left corner of the icon

explanation: Shortcut icons display a small curved arrow overlay, indicating that the icon is merely a pointer (.lnk file) to an executable file located elsewhere.

unit_title: Overview of Operating Systems, DOS & Windows Management
prompt: Which Windows accessory program is a lightweight, plain-text editor without rich formatting features, commonly used for editing code and batch scripts?
explanation: Notepad is the default ASCII/UTF-8 plain text editor in Windows that saves unformatted text files without font or paragraph markup.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: Before opening a PC cabinet to perform maintenance or upgrades, what vital safety precaution must be taken?

options.text: Unplug the AC power cord and ground yourself using an Anti-Static Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) wrist strap

explanation: Unplugging the power and using an ESD wrist strap discharges static electricity from the technician's body, preventing permanent microscopic damage to sensitive CMOS chips.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: What component inside the PC chassis converts high-voltage alternating current (AC) from the wall outlet into low-voltage direct current (DC) for internal components?
explanation: The SMPS converts 220V/110V AC mains voltage into regulated +12V, +5V, +3.3V, and -12V DC power lines required by motherboards, drives, and chips.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: On an ATX power supply connector, which color wire typically carries the +12V DC rail used for CPU and motor power?
explanation: Standard PC power wiring conventions use Yellow for +12V, Red for +5V, Orange for +3.3V, and Black for ground.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: During PC bootup, what firmware routine performs a hardware diagnostic self-test before attempting to boot the operating system?
explanation: POST checks the CPU registers, initializes the memory controller, validates RAM integrity, checks for video output, and verifies keyboard connection.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: If a desktop PC emits a continuous, repetitive beeping sequence upon powering on with no display output, the most probable hardware failure is:

options.text: RAM module unseated, faulty, or poorly contacted in its DIMM slot

explanation: Motherboard BIOS beep codes indicate hardware errors before video initialization; continuous beeping typically signals missing or unseated RAM modules.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: Thermal paste (thermal compound) is applied between the CPU integrated heat spreader (IHS) and the heatsink base primarily to:

options.text: Glue the CPU permanently to the socket
Eliminate microscopic air gaps and facilitate maximum thermal conduction between processor and cooler

explanation: Air is a terrible heat conductor; thermal paste fills microscopic surface imperfections, ensuring efficient heat transfer from the processor die to the heatsink.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: Which expansion slot standard provides point-to-point serial data transfer lanes (x1, x4, x8, x16) and is used for modern high-performance graphics cards?
explanation: PCIe replaced parallel PCI and AGP buses, using scalable serial lanes (e.g. PCIe x16) delivering tens of gigabytes per second bandwidth.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: The Northbridge chip on traditional motherboards historically managed communication between the CPU and:

options.text: High-speed devices: System RAM and the AGP/PCIe graphics card
Slow I/O ports: USB, SATA, and audio

explanation: The Northbridge was responsible for high-bandwidth tasks (memory controller, front-side bus, high-speed graphics), while the Southbridge handled slower peripheral I/O.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: What motherboard component contains CMOS setup configuration settings (date, time, boot priority) preserved by a coin-cell battery when the computer is unplugged?
explanation: A small 3V CR2032 lithium coin cell powers the CMOS RAM and Real-Time Clock chip so BIOS configuration parameters are not lost during power disconnection.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: Which standard form factor is the most widely adopted for modern consumer desktop motherboards and computer cases?
explanation: ATX (introduced by Intel in 1995) standardized motherboard dimensions (12 x 9.6 inches), port clusters, and integrated power control.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: Which display interface transmits uncompressed digital high-definition video AND multi-channel audio over a single cable?
explanation: HDMI carries both digital high-definition video and multi-channel surround sound on a single cable between computers, monitors, and televisions.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: The legacy blue 15-pin D-sub connector traditionally used to transmit analog video signals to CRT and early LCD monitors is:
explanation: VGA is an analog video standard using a 15-pin DE-15 connector, susceptible to signal degradation at long cable lengths compared to digital interfaces.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: The internal storage interface protocol designed from the ground up to unlock the high-speed potential of solid-state drives using PCIe lanes is:
explanation: NVMe bypasses legacy SATA controller bottlenecks by communicating directly with the CPU over high-speed PCIe lanes, achieving transfer rates exceeding 7,000 MB/s.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: On a mechanical hard disk drive, the time required for the read/write head assembly to physically reposition to the correct track is called:
explanation: Seek time is the physical mechanical duration needed to move the disk head actuator arm to the target concentric track on the spinning magnetic platter.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: Rotational latency of a hard disk refers to:

options.text: The time taken for the actuator arm to return to park position
The time taken for the target sector on the platter to rotate directly beneath the read/write head
The time taken to copy a file to USB
The spin-down time when shutting down

explanation: Rotational latency is the rotational delay while waiting for the requested disk sector to spin under the read head, averaging half the duration of one complete rotation.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: Standard single-layer DVD media offers a storage capacity of approximately:
explanation: A standard single-sided, single-layer DVD-ROM disc holds 4.7 GB of data, compared to 700 MB for a standard CD and 25 GB for a single-layer Blu-ray disc.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: Which standard Ethernet cable connector is used to connect network interface cards (NICs) to local area network switches and routers?
explanation: RJ-45 (Registered Jack 45) is an 8-pin modular connector standard utilized worldwide for twisted-pair Ethernet networking (Cat5e, Cat6, Cat6a).

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: What audio jack color on a standard PC motherboard audio backpanel is designated for stereo audio line-out (headphones or front speakers)?
explanation: PC 99 audio color-coding standards mandate Lime Green for stereo audio output, Pink for microphone input, and Light Blue for line-in audio.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: USB 3.0 ports are visually identified by which internal plastic tab color inside the connector?
explanation: USB 3.0 (SuperSpeed 5 Gbps) ports feature distinct bright Blue plastic insulator inserts to distinguish them from black USB 2.0 (480 Mbps) ports.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: The memory slot design utilized for installing RAM modules on desktop motherboards is known as:
explanation: Desktop systems utilize full-sized DIMM slots, whereas compact laptops and small form factor PCs utilize smaller SO-DIMMs (Small Outline DIMMs).

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: The Internet is fundamentally described as a:

options.text: Single centralized computer owned by the United Nations
Global decentralized network of interconnected computer networks communicating via TCP/IP protocols
Proprietary software program created by Microsoft

explanation: The Internet is a worldwide system of interconnected computer networks utilizing standardized Internet Protocol suite (TCP/IP) communication protocols.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: Who invented the World Wide Web (WWW) at CERN in 1989?
explanation: Sir Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web in 1989 by combining hypertext, uniform resource locators (URLs), and HTTP communication protocol.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: What is the crucial conceptual difference between the Internet and the World Wide Web?

options.text: The Internet and WWW are completely identical terms
The Internet is the underlying physical networking infrastructure; the Web is an information service operating on top of the Internet using HTTP
The Web is older than the Internet

explanation: The Internet is the global network hardware infrastructure; the World Wide Web is one of many application-layer services (alongside email, FTP, VoIP) running across it.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: In the URL 'https://www.example.com:8080/notes/bca.html', what does 'https' represent?

options.text: The transfer protocol (HyperText Transfer Protocol Secure)

explanation: The initial component before the '://' specifies the communication protocol scheme used to access the network resource.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: The primary function of the Domain Name System (DNS) is to:

options.text: Translate human-readable domain names (e.g. www.mjpru.ac.in) into machine-routable numerical IP addresses

explanation: DNS serves as the phonebook of the Internet, resolving alphanumeric domain names into numerical binary IP addresses so routers can route data packets.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: An IPv4 address consists of how many total bits?
explanation: IPv4 addresses are 32-bit binary numbers divided into four 8-bit octets separated by periods in dotted-decimal format (e.g., 192.168.1.1).

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: How many bits are used in an IPv6 address to overcome the exhaustion of IPv4 addresses?

options.text: 128 bits (represented as 8 groups of hexadecimal digits)

explanation: IPv6 utilizes 128-bit addresses (allowing 3.4 x 10^38 unique addresses), written as eight 16-bit blocks in hexadecimal format separated by colons.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: Which IPv4 address class is specifically reserved for Multicast groups?
explanation: IPv4 Class D addresses (range 224.0.0.0 to 239.255.255.255) are designated exclusively for multicasting data streams to multiple subscribed hosts.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: An organization that provides internet connectivity, routing, and access packages to individuals and companies is an:
explanation: Internet Service Providers (ISPs like Airtel, Jio, BSNL) provide telecom infrastructure, routing connections, and transit points to the global Internet backbone.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: Which software application reads, interprets, and renders HTML documents into interactive visual web pages on a user screen?
explanation: A Web Browser (Google Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge) parses HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to visually render multimedia web pages for users.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: A private internal corporate network that uses Internet protocols (TCP/IP, HTTP) accessible only by authorized internal employees is an:
explanation: An Intranet is a restricted internal enterprise network that leverages standard web technologies securely behind corporate firewalls for staff use.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: An Extranet differs from an Intranet because an Extranet:

options.text: Is open completely to the public worldwide
Extends controlled access of certain internal network resources to trusted external partners, suppliers, and vendors

explanation: An Extranet provides controlled, authenticated access to selected parts of an organization's intranet for external business partners and clients.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: Search engine web crawlers (also called Spiders or Bots) operate by:

options.text: Systematically browsing the World Wide Web, traversing hyperlinks, and indexing web page text and metadata into databases

explanation: Web crawlers autonomously fetch pages across hyperlinks, downloading contents to search engine indexing servers to update searchable search indices.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: In an email address format 'student@college.edu', what does 'college.edu' identify?

options.text: The personal username of the student
The domain name of the mail server hosting the mailbox

explanation: An email address separates the mailbox username from the destination mail server domain name using the '@' (at) symbol.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: Which network protocol is primarily responsible for transmitting outgoing electronic mail messages from a client to a mail server?
explanation: SMTP is the standard Internet push protocol for transferring outgoing mail from a client MUA to an MTA server and between relay mail servers.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: The POP3 (Post Office Protocol version 3) email retrieval protocol operates primarily by:

options.text: Keeping all emails permanently synced across multiple mobile devices
Downloading mail messages from the server to the local computer client and typically deleting them from the server

explanation: POP3 downloads email messages from the remote mail server to the user's local hard drive and removes them from the server mailbox by default.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: Why is IMAP (Internet Message Access Protocol) preferred over POP3 for modern mobile users?

options.text: IMAP is completely free while POP3 requires monthly fees
IMAP leaves email messages on the server, synchronizing mail folders and read/unread status across multiple devices simultaneously
IMAP does not use the Internet
IMAP only works with text messages

explanation: IMAP provides two-way folder synchronization, allowing users to view identical inbox states, sent items, and read statuses across phones, tablets, and laptops.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: In email headers, what is the key distinction between CC and BCC fields?

options.text: CC sends text only; BCC sends attachments
Recipients in CC are visible to all other recipients; email addresses in BCC (Blind Carbon Copy) remain invisible to all other recipients

explanation: BCC (Blind Carbon Copy) conceals recipient email addresses from everyone else on the recipient list, preserving recipient privacy.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: Unsolicited, mass-distributed bulk commercial advertising emails sent to thousands of recipients without consent are known as:
explanation: Spam refers to unwanted, unrequested bulk emails sent across mail relays, consuming server bandwidth and filling mailboxes.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: Netiquette refers to:

options.text: The mathematical protocol governing fiber optic pulses
The accepted code of polite, ethical, and professional behavior and etiquette observed when communicating online
The speed limit of broadband Internet
A software program for catching computer viruses

explanation: Netiquette (Network Etiquette) comprises common courtesy rules: avoiding ALL CAPS shouting, respecting privacy, avoiding flaming, and quoting context.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: The fraudulent attempt to obtain sensitive credentials (usernames, passwords, credit card numbers) by disguising as a trustworthy entity in an email is:
explanation: Phishing tricks victims into submitting confidential financial or login credentials on counterfeit web pages mimicking genuine institutions.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: What is the primary operational distinction between a 'Hacker' (White-Hat) and a 'Cracker' (Black-Hat)?

options.text: Hackers use Windows; Crackers use Linux
A White-Hat Hacker legally identifies vulnerabilities to help organizations patch defenses, whereas a Cracker maliciously exploits vulnerabilities for unauthorized personal gain or destruction

explanation: Ethical hackers (white-hat) operate with legal consent to enhance security, while crackers (black-hat) break into computer networks maliciously for theft or damage.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: A network security device that monitors and filters incoming and outgoing network traffic based on established security rule sets is a:
explanation: A Firewall acts as a protective barrier between a trusted internal network and untrusted external networks (like the Internet), inspecting packets.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: A Denial of Service (DoS) attack aims to:

options.text: Overwhelm a target server or network with excessive flood traffic, rendering it unavailable to legitimate users

explanation: DoS and DDoS attacks saturate network bandwidth or server compute resources with dummy request floods, causing services to crash or freeze for real users.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: Which security protocol secures HTTP traffic across the World Wide Web using Transport Layer Security (TLS/SSL) encryption?
explanation: HTTPS (HTTP over TLS/SSL) encrypts data transmitted between browser and web server, preventing eavesdropping and man-in-the-middle tampering.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: Strong password creation policies generally recommend all of the following EXCEPT:

options.text: Combining uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, and special symbols
Using common personal information like your birthdate or pet's name
Avoiding dictionary words and predictable patterns

explanation: Using names, birthdates, or predictable dictionary words leaves accounts vulnerable to simple dictionary and social engineering attacks.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: The criminal act of forging an email sender address so the message appears to originate from someone other than the actual source is called:
explanation: Email spoofing falsifies email header sender addresses (From:) because foundational SMTP protocols lacked built-in sender verification.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) enhances account security by requiring:

options.text: Two distinct authentication factors: something you know (password) and something you have (SMS code or hardware authenticator)
Logging in using two different web browsers

explanation: 2FA ensures that even if an attacker compromises a password, access remains blocked without the physical secondary token or biometric verification.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: Spyware is malware engineered specifically to:

options.text: Secretly monitor user activity, record keystrokes (keylogger), harvest browsing habits, and transmit data to third parties without consent

explanation: Spyware operates covertly in the background, intercepting passwords, financial transactions, and private messages without user awareness.

unit_title: PC Maintenance, Hardware, Motherboard & Internet Fundamentals
prompt: Under Indian law, cyber crimes and electronic commerce regulations are governed under which landmark legislation?

options.text: The Information Technology (IT) Act, 2000 (and subsequent amendments)

explanation: The Information Technology Act 2000 provides legal recognition for electronic transactions, digital signatures, and defines penal codes for cyber offenses.

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: What is the default file extension for documents saved in modern versions of Microsoft Word (Word 2007 and newer)?
explanation: Modern Word documents use the open XML-based .docx format, which reduces file size and improves data recovery compared to legacy binary .doc.

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: In Microsoft Word, standard default page margins on a blank document are:

options.text: 1.0 inch (2.54 cm) on top, bottom, left, and right
1.5 inches left and right, 1.0 inch top and bottom

explanation: The default 'Normal' margin setting in MS Word applies 1.0 inch (72 points or 2.54 cm) to Top, Bottom, Left, and Right margins.

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: What are the two standard page orientation modes available in word processing software?
explanation: Portrait orientates the page vertically (height greater than width); Landscape orientates the page horizontally (width greater than height).

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: The standard paper dimensions of an A4 sheet widely used in academic and technical document printing are:
explanation: A4 paper (ISO 216 standard) measures exactly 210 x 297 millimeters, whereas US Letter measures 8.5 x 11 inches (216 x 279 mm).

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: Which bar located at the very top of the Microsoft Word application window displays the active document name and window control buttons?
explanation: The Title Bar displays the current document filename (e.g. 'Document1 - Word') alongside Minimize, Maximize/Restore, and Close buttons.

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: The small toolbar located typically above the Ribbon that houses one-click shortcuts for Save, Undo, and Redo is the:
explanation: The Quick Access Toolbar is a customizable strip providing immediate access to frequently used commands regardless of which Ribbon tab is active.

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: Which keyboard shortcut combination is used in MS Word to instantly create a new blank document?
explanation: Pressing Ctrl + N spawns a new empty document window based on the Normal template.

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: To open an existing document in Microsoft Word, the standard shortcut key is:
explanation: Ctrl + O triggers the Open dialog or backstage view to browse and open saved document files.

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: The Status Bar located at the very bottom of the MS Word window displays:

options.text: Page numbers, word count, proofing language, view modes, and the zoom slider

explanation: The Status Bar provides real-time document metrics: Current Page, Total Pages, Word Count, Language, Read/Print/Web views, and Zoom percentage.

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: Which viewing mode in MS Word optimizes document display for reading on-screen by removing editing toolbars and showing pages as a book?
explanation: Read Mode maximizes screen area for reading, organizing text into horizontal reading columns and hiding Ribbon toolbars.

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: In MS Word, clicking three times rapidly inside a paragraph will select:
explanation: In Word: single click positions the cursor; double click selects a word; triple click selects the complete paragraph.

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: To select an entire document from start to finish using a keyboard shortcut, press:
explanation: Ctrl + A (Select All) highlights every element in the active document buffer, including text, graphics, and tables.

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: What is the keyboard shortcut to apply or remove Bold formatting on selected text?
explanation: Ctrl + B toggles bold font weighting on the active text selection.

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: Which formatting feature positions small text slightly below the normal baseline of text (as seen in chemical formulas like H2O)?
explanation: Subscript (Ctrl + =) lowers characters below the baseline; Superscript (Ctrl + Shift + Plus) raises them above the baseline (as in x^2).

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: To format mathematical exponents (e.g., x^2 or 1st), which feature raises text above the regular text baseline?
explanation: Superscript shifts selected characters above the normal baseline at a reduced font size.

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: The 'Format Painter' tool in Microsoft Word is used to:

options.text: Draw colorful shapes and clip art
Copy formatting attributes (font, size, color, paragraph styling) from selected text and paint them onto other text

explanation: Format Painter captures all styling properties of source text and applies them to destination text when brushed over.

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: Which Change Case option capitalizes the very first letter of every sentence while keeping all other letters lowercase?
explanation: Sentence case capitalizes the initial letter following sentence-ending punctuation (period, question mark), conforming to standard prose rules.

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: A decorative capital letter placed at the beginning of a paragraph that drops down across two or more lines of text is called a:
explanation: A Drop Cap creates an enlarged decorative initial letter that drops down into adjacent paragraph text lines, a classic typography styling.

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: What is the keyboard shortcut to center-align selected paragraph text in Microsoft Word?
explanation: Ctrl + E applies center alignment to the active paragraph (Ctrl + L is Left, Ctrl + R is Right, Ctrl + J is Justified).

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: Justified paragraph alignment in MS Word ensures that:

options.text: All text is aligned strictly against the left margin only
Text is adjusted by micro-spacing words so that both left and right edges align flush with margins
Text is centered on the page
Lines end in jagged right edges

explanation: Justify (Ctrl + J) adds subtle spacing between words so every full line touches both the left and right margins evenly.

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: In Word typography, a 'Hanging Indent' is defined as an indentation where:

options.text: All lines in the paragraph are indented equally
The first line begins at the left margin, and all subsequent lines in the paragraph are indented inward
Only the last line is indented
The paragraph is shifted to the right margin

explanation: A hanging indent (Ctrl + T) leaves the first line flush at the left margin while indenting subsequent lines (standard in bibliographies).

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: To insert a hard manual Page Break forcing following text onto a brand new page, press:
explanation: Ctrl + Enter inserts a hard Page Break character, whereas Shift + Enter inserts a Soft Line Break within the same paragraph.

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: What structural division in MS Word allows different sections of a single document to have different page orientations, headers, footers, or margins?
explanation: Section Breaks (e.g. Next Page, Continuous) partition a document into independent layouts with unique headers, numbering styles, or orientations.

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: Text or graphics (such as 'CONFIDENTIAL' or a company logo) appearing faintly behind document text on every page is called a:
explanation: A Watermark displays semi-transparent background text or imagery behind the foreground text for branding or classification.

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: Headers and Footers in Microsoft Word are used to:

options.text: Display recurring text, chapter titles, dates, or page numbers at the very top and bottom of pages throughout a document

explanation: Headers (top margin) and Footers (bottom margin) automatically repeat essential reference information and page numbers across all pages.

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: Which feature allows wrapping continuous text into multi-column formats (such as newspaper or research paper columns)?
explanation: The Columns tool under Page Setup splits text flow into two, three, or custom asymmetric vertical columns on the page.

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: What is the function of the 'Gutter Margin' in page layout?

options.text: Adding extra space to the top margin for titles
Adding additional margin space to the binding side of pages (inside or top) to accommodate bookbinding

explanation: Gutter margin adds extra clearance on the binding edge so text is not obscured when documents are stapled, bound, or hole-punched.

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: To display non-printing formatting characters (such as paragraph marks ¶, spaces ·, and tabs →), click the:
explanation: The Show/Hide (¶) toggle reveals hidden formatting characters, helping diagnose spacing irregularities and stray page breaks.

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: Which keyboard shortcut invokes the Find and Replace dialog directly focused on the 'Replace' tab?
explanation: Ctrl + H opens Find and Replace directly on the Replace tab (Ctrl + F opens Navigation Find; Ctrl + G opens Go To).

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: What built-in reference tool in MS Word provides lists of synonyms and antonyms for a selected word?
explanation: The Thesaurus tool suggests vocabulary alternatives, synonyms, and related linguistic terms for selected words.

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: In an MS Word table, pressing the 'Tab' key while positioned inside the very last cell of the table will:

options.text: Automatically insert a new empty row at the bottom of the table

explanation: Pressing Tab inside the final bottom-right table cell automatically appends a new empty row matching the column structure.

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: Combining two or more adjacent table cells into a single unified cell is known as:
explanation: Merge Cells consolidates multiple selected adjacent cells into one large cell, often used for table headings.

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: The keyboard shortcut to launch the full Spelling and Grammar check dialog across a Word document is:
explanation: Pressing F7 invokes the proofing engine to scan the document for misspelled words (red underline) and grammatical issues (blue underline).

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: Which feature in MS Word automatically corrects common typographical errors and misspellings as you type (e.g. changing 'teh' to 'the')?
explanation: AutoCorrect automatically replaces predefined misspelled strings or symbols with correct words immediately upon typing the spacebar.

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: What is the primary purpose of the 'Mail Merge' feature in Microsoft Word?

options.text: To convert Word documents into audio podcasts
To generate large batches of personalized letters, envelopes, or certificates by combining a template document with a data source
To scan documents for email viruses

explanation: Mail Merge marries a static master document template with dynamic database records (data source) to produce customized mass communications.

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: In a Mail Merge operation, the document containing the static letter body, logos, and merge field placeholders is called the:
explanation: The Main Document contains the common boilerplate text, layout, and placeholders («Name», «Address») that repeat for every record.

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: The file containing names, addresses, and variable student data in a Mail Merge operation (such as an Excel sheet or Access table) is the:
explanation: The Data Source is the structured database, spreadsheet, or contact table that feeds individual record values into the merge fields.

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: Placeholders inserted into a Mail Merge main document (such as «First_Name») where dynamic data will appear are called:
explanation: Merge Fields specify exact database column mapping points within the text where personalized data will be injected during output generation.

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: A Macro in Microsoft Word is:

options.text: A recorded series of commands, keystrokes, and instructions saved as a VBA script to automate repetitive tasks

explanation: A Macro records sequences of formatting or editing actions into Visual Basic for Applications (VBA) code, executable via shortcut or button.

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
