prompt: Which function key combination is used to view, run, or edit recorded Macros in Microsoft Word?
explanation: Alt + F8 opens the Macros dialog box displaying all available macros across active templates and documents.

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: What is the default presentation file extension used by Microsoft PowerPoint 2007 and newer?
explanation: Modern PowerPoint presentations save in the zipped XML-based .pptx file format.

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: To start a PowerPoint slide show from the very first slide, which function key is pressed?
explanation: Pressing F5 starts the presentation from Slide 1; pressing Shift + F5 starts the show from the currently active slide.

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: To launch a slide show starting directly from the CURRENT slide, the keyboard shortcut is:
explanation: Shift + F5 initiates the full-screen slide presentation starting immediately on the slide currently open in the editor.

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: Which PowerPoint view displays thumbnail images of all slides arranged in horizontal rows, ideal for reordering or deleting slides?
explanation: Slide Sorter view displays miniature thumbnails of all presentation slides, making drag-and-drop reorganization and transition setup effortless.

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: The top slide in a presentation hierarchy that stores overarching design templates, font themes, and logo placements for all child slides is the:
explanation: Slide Master dictates universal layout rules, backgrounds, footer placements, and typography globally across the entire presentation deck.

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: In PowerPoint, what is the crucial operational difference between an 'Animation' and a 'Transition'?

options.text: Animations only play on sound cards; transitions only play on monitors
A Transition is the visual entry effect between slides; an Animation is the movement applied to individual elements (text, pictures) within a slide
Transitions are for text; animations are for slides

explanation: Transitions control how an entire slide enters or exits the screen; Animations control the motion, entrance, or exit of specific objects on a slide.

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: Which of the following is NOT a standard category of object animation effects in Microsoft PowerPoint?
explanation: PowerPoint animation effects strictly comprise four classes: Entrance (green), Emphasis (yellow), Exit (red), and Motion Paths.

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: Which feature in PowerPoint allows a speaker to see the current slide, upcoming slide, elapsed timer, and private speaker notes on one monitor while the audience only sees full-screen slides on a projector?
explanation: Presenter View utilizes dual-monitor configurations to display private cues, notes, timers, and previews to the speaker while shielding them from audience view.

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: During a live PowerPoint presentation, pressing which key instantly turns the screen completely Black to pause and refocus audience attention?
explanation: Pressing the 'B' key toggles a black blank screen; pressing 'W' toggles a pure white blank screen during an active slide show.

unit_title: Word Processing (MS Word) & Presentation (MS PowerPoint)
prompt: The feature used to record spoken audio narration, laser pointer gestures, and exact slide transition timings for self-running presentations is:
explanation: Record Slide Show / Rehearse Timings captures precise narration, on-screen ink pen annotations, and slide pacing for automated replay.

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: An electronic spreadsheet file in Microsoft Excel containing one or more worksheets is called a:
explanation: In Excel, the entire file (.xlsx) is called a Workbook, which acts as a binder containing one or multiple individual Worksheets.

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: In Microsoft Excel 2016 / 2019 / 365, what is the maximum number of rows available in a single worksheet?
explanation: Modern Excel worksheets offer exactly 1,048,576 rows (numbered 1 to 1,048,576) and 16,384 columns (labeled A to XFD).

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: What is the column heading label of the very last column in a modern Excel worksheet?
explanation: The 16,384th and final column in modern Excel worksheets is designated with the letter header XFD.

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: The intersection of a row and a column in an Excel worksheet is called a:
explanation: A Cell is the fundamental unit of storage in a spreadsheet, identified by its column letter and row number (e.g., C5).

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: Which small box located to the left of the Formula Bar displays the address of the currently active cell (e.g. A1)?
explanation: The Name Box displays the active cell reference or the name of a selected range and allows jumping directly to any typed coordinate.

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: Every formula and function in Microsoft Excel must strictly begin with which mathematical symbol?
explanation: Excel requires the equals sign (=) at the start of a cell entry to instruct the calculation engine to parse and evaluate the following string as a formula.

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: The Formula Bar in Microsoft Excel is used to:

options.text: Display the file size of the workbook
View, enter, or edit the underlying formula or actual data content stored in the active cell

explanation: The Formula Bar displays the actual formula or text of the selected cell, while the cell on the sheet displays the computed result.

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: What small black square handle in the lower-right corner of an active cell boundary is dragged to copy formulas or extend data series?
explanation: The Fill Handle (AutoFill) detects patterns (numbers, weekdays, dates) and copies formulas or extrapolates series when dragged across rows/columns.

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: To instantly sum an adjacent continuous column or row of numbers in Excel, which shortcut key combination invokes AutoSum?
explanation: Pressing Alt + = automatically generates the =SUM() formula selecting the adjacent numerical range above or to the left.

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: If an Excel cell displays a string of hash symbols '######', what does this indicate?

options.text: A catastrophic formula error has corrupted the sheet
The column is too narrow to display the numerical or date value in the current format
The cell has been locked with a password

explanation: A '######' display simply means the cell column width is insufficient to render the full formatted number or date; expanding column width resolves it.

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: Which type of cell reference automatically adjusts its row and column coordinates when copied from one cell to another?
explanation: Relative references (e.g. A1) store offsets relative to the formula's position; copying the formula down shifts row numbers accordingly.

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: Which symbol is used in Excel to lock a column or row coordinate into an Absolute Cell Reference (e.g. $A$1)?
explanation: The dollar sign ($) locks coordinates so that row numbers or column letters remain fixed regardless of where the formula is copied.

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: In the formula '=$B$4 * C2', what will happen to the reference '$B$4' when the formula is copied down three rows?
explanation: Because both column B and row 4 are anchored with dollar signs ($), the reference $B$4 remains completely unchanged when copied.

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: A cell reference where either the row is locked or the column is locked, but not both (such as '$A1' or 'A$1'), is a:
explanation: Mixed references lock only one dimension: $A1 locks the column while row varies; A$1 locks the row while column varies.

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: Which function key on the keyboard is used while editing a formula in Excel to cycle through relative, absolute, and mixed reference formats ($A$1 -> A$1 -> $A1 -> A1)?
explanation: Pressing F4 while a cell reference is selected in the formula bar cycles cyclically through all four absolute and mixed reference combinations.

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: A 3D reference in Microsoft Excel refers to:

options.text: A formula reference that spans across multiple worksheets in a workbook (e.g. =SUM(Sheet1:Sheet3!B5))
A reference to a 3D bar chart

explanation: A 3D reference calculates data across an identical cell or range across multiple contiguous worksheets.

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: If cell A1 contains 10 and cell A2 contains 20, what will the formula '=A1 + A2 * 2' evaluate to according to standard arithmetic precedence?
explanation: Multiplication takes precedence over addition: (20 * 2) = 40; then 10 + 40 = 50.

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: Which mathematical operator in Excel is used to calculate powers or exponentiation (e.g. 2 cubed)?
explanation: The caret symbol (^) computes exponentiation (e.g., =2^3 evaluates to 8).

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: The string concatenation operator used in Excel to join two text strings together (e.g. =A1 & " " & B1) is the:
explanation: The ampersand (&) operator concatenates text values together, serving as a formula alternative to the CONCATENATE() function.

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: In an Excel formula, a colon (:) placed between two cell references (such as 'A1:C10') denotes:

options.text: A contiguous rectangular range of cells from the top-left cell to the bottom-right cell

explanation: The colon range operator specifies all cells enclosed within the rectangular boundary defined by the two corner coordinates.

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: Which Excel function returns the mathematical remainder after dividing a number by a divisor?
explanation: The MOD(number, divisor) function returns the remainder resulting from integer division (e.g. =MOD(10, 3) returns 1).

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: To round a numerical value to a specified number of decimal places in Excel, use the function:
explanation: The ROUND(number, num_digits) function rounds a value mathematically to the specified number of decimal places.

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: What is the crucial difference between the 'COUNT()' function and the 'COUNTA()' function in Excel?

options.text: COUNT counts all cells; COUNTA counts only negative numbers
COUNT counts only cells containing numbers; COUNTA counts all non-empty cells (numbers, text, logical values)
COUNT counts formulas; COUNTA counts text only

explanation: COUNT() strictly tallies cells containing numerical data; COUNTA() (Count All) tallies any cell that is not blank.

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: Which Excel function counts the number of cells within a specified range that satisfy a given criteria or condition?
explanation: COUNTIF(range, criteria) evaluates cells against a test condition (e.g. =COUNTIF(B2:B50, ">75")) and tallies matching instances.

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: The function that calculates the arithmetic mean of a range of values in Excel is:
explanation: The AVERAGE() function calculates the sum of all numerical arguments divided by the count of numbers in the range.

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: Which statistical function identifies and returns the single middle value in an ordered set of numbers?
explanation: MEDIAN() returns the statistical midpoint of a numeric dataset where half the values are above and half are below.

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: To return the most frequently occurring value in a data range in Excel, the appropriate function is:
explanation: The MODE() function identifies the most frequently recurring numerical value in a sample dataset.

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: Which function returns the current system date and current time, updating dynamically whenever the worksheet recalculates?
explanation: The NOW() function takes no arguments and returns the dynamic current system date and timestamp; TODAY() returns only the date without time.

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: What does the formula '=TODAY()' output in an Excel cell?

options.text: The time of day in milliseconds
The current calendar date according to the computer system clock
The day of the week as text
The date the workbook was originally created

explanation: The volatile function TODAY() outputs the current date formatted as DD/MM/YYYY or MM/DD/YYYY without a time component.

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: To calculate the square root of a positive number in cell B4, the formula is:
explanation: The SQRT(number) function computes the positive square root of a numerical argument.

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: In an Excel '=IF(C2 >= 40, "Pass", "Fail")' formula, what will be returned if cell C2 contains the value 38?
explanation: Because the condition 38 >= 40 evaluates to FALSE, the IF function returns its third argument, which is "Fail".

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: Which logical function in Excel returns TRUE only if ALL of its individual argument conditions evaluate to TRUE?
explanation: The AND(cond1, cond2, ...) function evaluates multiple logical tests and returns TRUE only when every single condition is satisfied.

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: The logical function that returns TRUE if AT LEAST ONE of its argument conditions evaluates to TRUE is:
explanation: The OR() function returns TRUE if any one of its supplied logical tests evaluates to TRUE, returning FALSE only if all are false.

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: Which text function removes all irregular leading, trailing, and duplicate spaces from a text string, leaving only single spaces between words?
explanation: TRIM() cleans text imported from other applications by eliminating extraneous spaces while preserving standard single word spacing.

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: To convert a text string in cell A1 into proper title casing (where the first letter of each word is capitalized), use:
explanation: PROPER() capitalizes the first character of each word and converts all subsequent characters to lowercase.

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: What does the VLOOKUP function in Excel perform?

options.text: Searches for a lookup value in the first column of a table array and returns a value in the same row from a specified column index
Converts vertical text into horizontal rows

explanation: VLOOKUP (Vertical Lookup) searches down the leftmost column of a table to find a matching key and retrieves data from an adjacent column.

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: In the formula '=VLOOKUP(101, A2:D50, 3, FALSE)', the final argument 'FALSE' specifies:

options.text: That negative numbers should be ignored

explanation: The range_lookup parameter FALSE (or 0) instructs VLOOKUP to seek an exact match, returning #N/A if the exact lookup value is absent.

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: Which Excel error code is displayed when a formula attempts to divide a number by zero or by an empty blank cell?
explanation: #DIV/0! explicitly signals an illegal division by zero or a reference to an empty cell treated as zero in a denominator.

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: The '#NAME?' error in an Excel formula indicates:

options.text: A cell reference is invalid because a row/column was deleted
Excel does not recognize text in the formula, typically caused by a misspelled function name (e.g. =SMM() instead of =SUM())
A number is divided by zero
A value is missing from a VLOOKUP table

explanation: #NAME? occurs when Excel cannot resolve a named token, almost always caused by a typographical error in a function name or missing quotes around a text string.

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: The '#REF!' error code in an Excel formula signifies that:

options.text: The formula contains an invalid cell reference, typically caused when referenced cells or columns were deleted
A number is too large to display

explanation: #REF! (Reference Error) occurs when a formula references a cell coordinate that has been permanently deleted from the worksheet grid.

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: Which feature in Excel keeps top header rows or leftmost columns visible on screen while scrolling through long worksheets?
explanation: Freeze Panes (View tab) locks selected rows or columns in place so table column headers remain visible as users scroll down thousands of records.

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: What Excel tool restricts the type of data or values that users can enter into a specific cell (e.g., allowing only whole numbers between 1 and 100, or a dropdown list)?
explanation: Data Validation sets input constraints (number ranges, dates, custom lists, text lengths) and displays customizable error alerts upon invalid entry.

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: Which feature automatically applies background colors, font colors, or icon sets to cells when their values meet specific rules or thresholds?
explanation: Conditional Formatting dynamically highlights trends (e.g. red for failing scores, green for high performers) based on cell values.

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: To display data sorted in alphabetical order (A to Z) or numeric order (Smallest to Largest), which tool on the Data tab is used?
explanation: The Sort tool arranges selected records ascending (A-Z, 0-9) or descending (Z-A, 9-0) across single or multiple sorting hierarchy levels.

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: AutoFilter in Excel is identified by:

options.text: Red warning borders around the worksheet
Small dropdown arrows appearing in the header row of each data column allowing instant filtering and sorting

explanation: Activating Filter (Ctrl + Shift + L) places clickable dropdown arrows in table headers to filter by value, color, or condition.

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: Which chart type in Microsoft Excel is best suited for showing the proportional contribution of individual parts to an entire whole (percentages of 100%)?
explanation: Pie charts display proportional shares of a categorical total, representing slices of a circular disk summing to 100%.

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: To visualize continuous trends, fluctuations, and changes in data over a continuous time series, the most appropriate chart type is a:
explanation: Line charts connect sequential data points along a continuous scale, ideally illustrating performance, sales, or temperature changes over time.

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: In an Excel chart, what component explains the meaning of various data series, colors, or patterns used in the visualization?
explanation: The Legend provides an explanatory key identifying the categories, colors, or markers assigned to different data series in the plot area.

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: A Macro in Microsoft Excel is written in which underlying programming language?
explanation: Excel macros are recorded and executed using Microsoft's Visual Basic for Applications (VBA) macro programming environment.

unit_title: Spreadsheet (MS Excel) - Formulas, Functions & Macros
prompt: What file extension must an Excel workbook be saved with to preserve and permit execution of embedded VBA Macros?
explanation: Excel Macro-Enabled Workbooks must be saved with the .xlsm extension; standard .xlsx workbooks automatically strip all macro code for security.
